questions.q: A writer can't pitch their script in two sentences. What would Snyder say to do first?
choices: Find the inciting incident
Write the logline before anything else
Outline it as eight sequences
Time a few films in the same genre
questions.explain: Snyder's first chapter asks 'what is it?' If you can't pitch it, you probably don't know what it is.

questions.q: What should happen at Snyder's Midpoint?
choices: The hero chooses to enter the new world
The theme is stated
A false victory or false defeat, and the stakes are raised
The hero returns to the familiar world, changed
questions.explain: At page 55, Fun and Games ends with a false win or loss, and the story gets serious.

questions.q: How should the Opening Image and Final Image relate?
choices: They should be identical, showing nothing has changed
The Final Image should introduce a sequel
As opposites, so together they show how the hero has changed
They should both feature the villain
questions.explain: Put them side by side and you should see the whole arc.

questions.q: A thriller has both aliens and time travel. Which Snyder rule does it break?
choices: The Pope in the Pool
Laying Pipe
Covenant of the Arc
Double Mumbo Jumbo
questions.explain: Audiences will accept one piece of magic per movie, not two.

questions.q: Where does the B Story usually come in, and what does it carry?
choices: Around page 30, often a love story that carries the theme
On page 1, carrying the backstory
At the climax, carrying the twist
After the Final Image, carrying the sequel hook
questions.explain: The B Story starts as the hero enters Act Two, and meets the A story at Break into Three.

questions.q: Which critique did Peter Suderman make in Slate in 2013?
choices: That Snyder ignored the second act
That blockbusters were following the beat sheet so closely they all felt alike
That the beat sheet was stolen from Aristotle
That Snyder's genres were too few
questions.explain: Snyder's defenders replied that the beats describe what worked before the book existed.

questions.q: Why does Snyder sort films into ten genres such as Monster in the House and Golden Fleece?
choices: To decide the budget
So each genre can have its own page count
To avoid writing a B story
So writers know what audiences enjoyed before in that kind of story and give it 'the same, only different'
questions.explain: His genres are story shapes, not marketing labels.

ideas: Early on, the hero should do something that makes the audience want to root for them.
Fifteen beats, each with a target page in a 110-page script, from Opening Image to Final Image.
Audiences will swallow one piece of magic per movie, but not two.
Sort your film by its story type, like Monster in the House or Golden Fleece, and give the audience the same, only different.
